question: Many Canadians say writer and rider with the same quick flapped middle consonant. What still tells the two words apart?
options: A faint t kept in writer
answer: The vowel before the flap. Canadian English raises the vowel of write before voiceless sounds such as t, and writer keeps that raised vowel even after its t has turned into the flap it shares with rider. The same raising gives about its Canadian vowel, which is not the aboot of the jokes.
move: When two things match at one point, look at what came just before.
trap: Assuming words with identical consonants must end up sounding identical.
reference: Chambers, Canadian Raising, Canadian Journal of Linguistics 18(2), 1973
